layering.description: billing_calculation_service.py has zero imports beyond Types/stdlib (pure function, no Repository/Config); registration_service.py and plan_catalog_service.py import Types/Config/Repository/logging_service only, no API imports.

typing.description: mypy --strict clean on all of backend/src; no `Any` usage; billing_calculation_service.py uses Decimal exclusively, no float (E4-S2 AC-4).

folder_structure.description: service/registration_service.py, service/plan_catalog_service.py, service/billing_calculation_service.py exist, plus one test file each; repository/subscriber_repository.py gained get_active_subscription_by_mobile, repository/plan_repository.py gained update_draft_plan_version, types/exceptions.py gained InvalidMobileNumberError/DuplicateActiveSubscriptionError/PlanVersionImmutableError, service/logging_service.py's PII_FIELD_NAMES gained identity_proof_ref.

env_vars.description: No new environment variables introduced in Group C.

migrations.description: No schema.sql changes in Group C — all three stories operate on tables/columns already created in Group B.

test_checks.description: Registering with a valid mobile number, identity-proof reference, and plan type creates a subscription in PENDING_KYC state, and both rows are persisted.
Registering a mobile number that already has an ACTIVE subscription is rejected with a specific error (DuplicateActiveSubscriptionError), not a generic failure.
Registering with a malformed mobile number is rejected before any database write (parametrized over multiple malformed examples — 5 collected items for this one test name).
identity_proof_ref is persisted in full but masked when logged.
Creating a new plan starts an unpublished draft version at version number 1.
Publishing a draft marks it published=true and it becomes the version returned by get_published_version.
Attempting to edit a published version's price raises PlanVersionImmutableError rather than succeeding.
Requesting a change to a published plan creates a new incremented draft version, leaving the prior published version unchanged and retrievable.

Only an admin-role principal can create, publish, or update a plan version; a non-admin attempt is rejected for all three operations (one of the three test names is parametrized over 2 non-admin roles, so 3 named tests collect as 4 items).

A plan change exactly at a billing-cycle boundary produces a pro-rata charge of 0.00 (scenario 1 of the table-driven parametrized test — the full parametrized test is run since a single case cannot be cleanly selected by name; scenario 1 is change_date == cycle_end -> 0.00, asserted alongside the other 5).

A plan change mid-cycle in non-leap-year February (2026, 28 days) and leap-year February (2028, 29 days) both produce correct, distinct pro-rata amounts (scenarios 2 and 3 of the same parametrized test as grp-c-10 — shared evidence, same command/expected).
The calculated charge is always >= 0, including a downgrade scenario whose raw differential is negative (NFR-08).
All intermediate and final amounts are Decimal typed; no float is used anywhere in the calculation module.

A unit test table-drives at least 6 boundary-date scenarios (including the leap-year case) and asserts exact expected Decimal values (same parametrized test as grp-c-10/grp-c-11 — this feature is about the test's coverage breadth, satisfied by the same 6-item table).
Full backend test suite, lint, and strict typecheck all clean together (regression gate covering Groups A+B+C combined).
